full_judgment: 10. It has however been pleaded before this Court by the learned Advocate for Mr. Habibullah Khan while contesting this suo moto Rule that in any proceeding under Article 102 of the Constitution costs cannot be awarded against a third party who was not a party in the original Writ Petition. So far as the provisions of Article 102 of the Constitution is concerned, there is nothing to indicate therein as to when and how, to whom and against whom costs shall be awarded. This has been provided in rules 14 and 15 relating to the Writ Petitions contained in Appendix IV (A) of Rules of the High Court as mentioned hereinbefore. So far as the costs that may be awarded against any party is concerned it has been kept open in the aforesaid Rules and it is to be decided by the Court in the facts and circumstances of each case. The only limitation inevitably would be that no cost shall be awarded against any party finally if such party was not a party in the concerned 'A writ Petition unless such party is given a notice to show cause why such party shall not be saddled with costs and the reply thereto is heard and considered in due course.
